channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund Reports Surplus Amid Budget Dependence
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund ended 2025 with a surplus of approximately 3 billion soms, but remains dependent on state budget funding for pension obligations. A deputy noted that despite a pension increase, purchasing power decreased due to rising prices.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President visits Utah Olympic Park, studies winter sports development
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov visited Utah Olympic Park during his US trip. He met with the 2034 Winter Olympics organizing committee chair and learned about sports infrastructure development and legacy use. Japarov expressed interest in Utah's experience with popularizing winter sports among youth and tourism.

item.title: Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon begins working trip to Sughd region
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has started a working trip to the Sughd region on September 20. The purpose is to inaugurate facilities, assess the socio-economic situation, meet residents, and participate in events celebrating the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence. He was welcomed at Khujand International Airport.

item.title: Interpol identifies 126 terrorists using AI in Operation Shams II
item.description: Interpol identified 126 foreign fighters using artificial intelligence during Operation Shams II, an anti-terrorism effort targeting digital networks. The operation, led by Interpol with specialists from 11 countries, analyzed over 108,000 images shared by jihadists. AI tools helped remove duplicates and enhance image quality, reducing the dataset for facial recognition.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocated 18.3 trillion soums in mortgage loans over 8 months
item.description: In Uzbekistan, 18.3 trillion soums were allocated for mortgage loans in the first eight months of the year. The primary market accounted for 74% of these loans. Data also revealed the age distribution of borrowers and the proportion of men and women among them.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan faces growing pension burden as contributors decline
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is experiencing a decrease in insurance contribution payers while the number of pensioners rises, according to Social Fund data. The ratio has fallen to 1.8 payers per pensioner, raising concerns about budget strain. The real purchasing power of pensions has also declined despite a nominal increase.

item.title: Seven detained after mass brawl outside Osh nightclub
item.description: Police detained seven individuals following a mass brawl outside the '03222' nightclub in Osh. The incident occurred on September 19, and video footage circulated on social media. One participant, born in 2004, sustained injuries and sought medical attention. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Iran Submits Peace Proposal to US via Qatar to End Conflict, Awaiting Trump's Response
item.description: Iran has submitted its proposal to the United States aimed at ending the conflict. The peace initiative was conveyed to Washington through Qatari mediation. A response from former President Trump is currently anticipated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Meets Utah Governor and Senate Leadership During US Visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Utah Governor Spencer Cox and Senate leader Stuart Adams in Salt Lake City. They discussed expanding cooperation in economic, investment, and cultural spheres, focusing on mining, tourism, and IT.

item.title: Central Asian Glaciers Shrinking, Reducing Water Supply, Study Finds
item.description: Glaciers in Central Asia are diminishing, leading to a significant decrease in water inflow to reservoirs in Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Afghanistan, according to a study by the World Meteorological Organization.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Compensates Doctors in Scarce Specialties, Addresses Textbook Shortages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's government is providing monthly compensation of 22,222 soms to doctors in deficit specialties outside Bishkek and Osh. Interns and residents outside major cities will receive 20,000 soms. Meanwhile, discussions intensify over textbook shortages and high prices, with the state printing house denying responsibility for books sold on the black market.

item.title: Karalkalpakstan's economy shows rapid growth with significant investment and energy sector development
item.description: Karalkalpakstan's economy grew 10.2% in the first half of the year, ranking second nationally. Significant investments, totaling $1.7 billion last year, and tax incentives have fueled this growth. The region also boosted its green energy capacity, with wind power contributing 23% to its electricity generation.

item.title: 17-year-old apprehended in Chirchiq while receiving a hashish-laden package from Russia
item.description: A 17-year-old in Chirchiq, Tashkent region, was arrested while receiving a package containing 852.2 grams of hashish from Russia. The Customs Committee reported the operation, conducted with security services, found the drugs hidden in four cans. Equipment potentially used for drug packaging was also seized.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Armenia strengthen cooperation in legal information
item.description: Uzbekistan and Armenia are enhancing cooperation in legal information exchange. A delegation from Armenia's Ministry of Justice visited the National Legal Information Center 'Adolat' in Uzbekistan. They signed a memorandum of understanding to develop bilateral ties, improve legal databases, and expand translation and publication of legislative acts.

item.title: Pakistan mosque blast death toll rises to 31
item.description: The death toll from a mosque explosion in Pakistan has risen to 31, with over 100 injured in the suicide bombing and subsequent armed clashes. An operation to eliminate militants hiding in a police building is ongoing. A group linked to Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility.

item.title: UNDP supports development of Jogorku Kenesh strategy until 2031
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh (Kyrgyzstan's parliament) will develop a strategy until 2031 with support from the UN Development Programme (UNDP). The document aims to improve lawmaking quality, strengthen parliamentary oversight, and digitalize processes, including the use of artificial intelligence.

item.title: SCO anti-drug operation 'Web' concludes in Kyrgyzstan with significant seizures
item.description: An international headquarters for the SCO anti-drug operation 'Web' concluded in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region. The operation involved 25,000 law enforcement officers across SCO states, resulting in over 3,800 drug crimes detected, 811 arrests, and the seizure of 5.3 tons of narcotics and precursors.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan to accelerate joint oil and gas projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan will accelerate the implementation of joint investment projects in the oil and gas sector. This was discussed in Baku by energy ministers and SOCAR's head. Discussions focused on practical results from recent leader meetings and transforming energy agreements into concrete projects. The treaty of eternal friendship was highlighted as a new stage in bilateral relations.

item.title: Overdue bank loans surge, with state banks holding over 70% of problem debt
item.description: Loans overdue for repayment to banks have sharply increased. State banks account for over 70% of these problem loans. However, private banks have seen a faster growth in the volume of loans that could not be collected on time.

item.title: Belarus and Kyrgyzstan approve mutual recognition of driver's licenses
item.description: Belarus and Kyrgyzstan have approved a mutual recognition agreement for driver's licenses in Minsk. This will introduce a simplified exchange procedure, beneficial for long-term residents or those planning to work. The agreement allows for the exchange of licenses without theoretical or practical tests after obtaining permanent residency.

item.title: India officially permits import of pomegranates and peppers from Uzbekistan
item.description: India has officially authorized the import of pomegranates and peppers from Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan is also working to establish a "green corridor" to simplify the import of pineapples and papayas from India.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan doubles berry exports to Russia's Perm Krai
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has doubled its strawberry and raspberry exports to Russia's Perm Krai region this year. Over 117.2 tons of berries have been imported from Kyrgyzstan since the start of the year, a 1.9-fold increase compared to the previous year. No quarantine pests were found in the shipments.

item.title: US Military AI Use Nearly Led to War with China, CNN Reports
item.description: US military personnel almost intercepted a Chinese vessel in spring 2026 based on faulty AI-generated data, CNN reported, citing four sources. The AI incorrectly identified a ship in the Middle East as carrying nuclear program components. The operation was halted after officials reviewed the AI's analysis, which was deemed "completely wrong."

item.title: US military AI error nearly triggered war with China, report says
item.description: US military personnel almost intercepted a Chinese vessel in 2026 based on faulty AI-generated intelligence, according to CNN. The AI, analyzing data via a chatbot, incorrectly identified the cargo of a ship in the Middle East, leading to preparations for an interception that could have escalated into conflict.

item.title: Dozens killed and injured in ongoing clashes between US and Iran
item.description: Dozens of people have been killed and injured amid ongoing exchanges of fire between the United States and Iran. The two countries continue their attacks on each other's regions.

item.title: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Boobek Ajikeev arrested pending investigation
item.description: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Boobek Ajikeev has been arrested pending investigation. The court ordered his detention until November 18. He is accused of abuse of office related to violations during the construction of a building near the Ala-Archa river.

item.title: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister arrested pending investigation
item.description: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Boobek Ajikeev has been detained pending investigation. The Pervomaysky District Court in Bishkek approved the request from investigative bodies. Ajikeev faces charges of abuse of official position. He will remain in custody until November 18. The arrest follows revelations of construction violations at a meteorological station.

item.title: Uzbekistan covers tuition for over 11,000 female master's students in six months
item.description: In six months, Uzbekistan has covered the tuition fees for over 11,000 female master's students. The state allocated a total of 75.5 billion UZS from the budget for these payments, a 57.3% increase compared to the previous year.

item.title: Uzbekistan to establish 30,000 hectares of salt-resistant orchards in Karakalpakstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish 30,000 hectares of salt-resistant plum and late apricot plantations in Karakalpakstan over three years. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the program, which will begin this year on 10,000 hectares. The project aims to create 20,000 jobs and increase fruit exports to $500 million within three years.

item.title: North Korea Rejects UN Nuclear Watchdog Resolution, Citing Irreversible Nuclear State Status
item.description: North Korea has rejected a resolution from the UN's nuclear watchdog organization. Pyongyang stated that its status as a nuclear state is irreversible and secured by its nuclear deterrence capabilities. The country maintains its nuclear program is a result of its security needs.

item.title: Chairman of Karakalpakstan's Jokargy Kenes Awarded Major General Rank
item.description: Amanbay Orinbayev, Chairman of the Jokargy Kenes (parliament) of Karakalpakstan, has been awarded the rank of Major General. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented the rank for Orinbayev's extensive service in law enforcement and contributions to Karakalpakstan's development and public welfare.

item.title: Interest Rate for Family Entrepreneurship Loans in Karakalpakstan to Decrease to 12%
item.description: The interest rate for family entrepreneurship loans in Karakalpakstan will be reduced from 17.5% to 12%. This initiative aims to support at least 30,000-40,000 more entrepreneurs. A 300 billion soum credit line at 16% will be opened for reliable customers, with the Entrepreneurship Development Company covering 4% of the interest.

item.title: Group facilitating illegal SAT exam test-taking for others apprehended in Tashkent
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent have dismantled a group, largely composed of university students, that facilitated illegal SAT certificate acquisition. The group operated a "bunker" where individuals remotely solved test questions for candidates. One member charged $1,500 per certificate, receiving payment via cryptocurrency.

item.title: US military nearly attacked Chinese ship due to AI error, CNN reports
item.description: US military personnel nearly attacked a Chinese vessel due to an artificial intelligence error, CNN reported, citing a US military intelligence analyst. The AI incorrectly concluded the ship was transporting components for Iran's nuclear program by combining open-source and classified data.

item.title: Group facilitating illegal SAT certificate acquisition exposed in Tashkent
item.description: A group in Tashkent has been exposed for illegally facilitating SAT certificate acquisition. The suspects reportedly set up a 'bunker' in a private school building to complete test questions on behalf of applicants. Further details were provided via a link to the Daryo.uz report.

item.title: Uzbekistan to purchase 10 Škoda electric trains for Tashkent suburban routes
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to acquire 10 Škoda 25Ev electric trains for 157 million euros to operate on Tashkent's suburban routes. The project, approved by the Tashkent City Council, is scheduled for implementation between 2026 and 2030.

item.title: Uzbek President tasks regional governors with developing Karakalpakstan neighborhoods
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has assigned regional governors the task of developing neighborhoods they are responsible for in Karakalpakstan. The proposal was made to name streets and neighborhoods after the regions that improved them if residents approve.

item.title: Chinese agricultural delegation explores agricultural potential in Tajikistan's Dangara district
item.description: A delegation from China's Ministry of Agriculture visited Tajikistan's Dangara district to explore agricultural potential and discuss expanding cooperation. Discussions focused on investment, modern technologies, and increasing agricultural exports between the two countries.

item.title: Karakalpakstan to become a major center for "green" energy production, says president
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced that Karakalpakstan is set to become a major hub for "green" energy production. New energy capacities totaling 860 MW have been commissioned, increasing electricity generation fourfold. Green energy's share in total production reached 23%.

item.title: Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service to launch in March next year
item.description: The Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service is scheduled to commence in March of the following year. Additionally, projects worth $8 billion in artificial intelligence and data centers are planned for Qoraqalpog‘iston.
